title: Detailed Study of Stars and Gas in a z = 8.3 Massive Merger with Extreme Dust Conditions
question: What are the resolved physical properties, star formation histories, and ISM conditions of the z = 8.312 massive galaxy MACS0416-Y1, and what drives its extreme dust temperature?

what.value: ALMA Band 7 (353 GHz) data and continuum mean size, 353 GHz continuum emission, 260 GHz upper limit, and [O III] 88 μm line luminosity (0.66 ± 0.16 Jy km s^-1)

evidence.quote: We use all the data presented in Table 1 of Y. Tamura et al. (2023) to reproduce the contours of the continuum emission in ALMA Band 7 (B7) at 353 GHz (Figure 1).

evidence.loc: 2.5. Cold Dust Spectral Energy Distribution Fitting
evidence.quote: We perform a fit of the cold dust spectral energy distribution (SED) using the continuum emission detected at 465 and 353 GHz from Y. Tamura et al. (2019) and the stringent 3σ upper limit at 200 GHz from T. J. L. C. Bakx et al. (2020).

evidence.loc: 3.2. Physical Properties with Emission Line Ratios
evidence.quote: We use the L [O III]λ88 μm = 0.66 ± 0.16 Jy km s −1 from Y. Tamura et al. (2019).

external_data.citation: Y. Tamura et al. (2019), Y. Tamura et al. (2023)

evidence.loc: 2.5. Cold Dust Spectral Energy Distribution Fitting
evidence.quote: We perform a fit of the cold dust spectral energy distribution (SED) using the continuum emission detected at 465 and 353 GHz from Y. Tamura et al. (2019) and the stringent 3σ upper limit at 200 GHz from T. J. L. C. Bakx et al. (2020).

what.value: Molecular gas mass estimated using [C II] dynamical decomposition and lower-frequency radio observations

evidence.quote: Given the multiwavelength observations of MACS0416-Y1 and taking the estimate of molecular gas mass (estimated using [C II ] dynamical decomposition) from G. C. Jones et al. (2024b)

evidence.loc: 2.5. Cold Dust Spectral Energy Distribution Fitting
evidence.quote: MACS0416-Y1 also has shallow observations at lower frequencies (see also G. C. Jones et al. 2024b).

what.value: Cluster-scale gravitational lens model for MACS0416

evidence.quote: For the magnification estimate, we use the cluster-scale lens model presented in G. Rihtaršič et al. (2024), constructed with public lens modeling software Lenstool (E. Jullo et al. 2007).

recipe.goal: Reduce JWST NIRCam imaging and extract resolved clump and halo photometry
recipe.method: Reduce NIRCam data using modified STScI pipeline, align to HST ACS, drizzle to 0.04'' pixel scale, detect sources, and fit 3 point sources (clumps) + 1 Sérsic profile (halo) in 7''x7'' cutouts across 6 bands
key_parameters: jwst_0916.pmap CRDS_CTX, 0.04'' pixel scale, 7'' x 7'' cutouts
assumptions: Three clumps modeled as point sources (and later Sérsic profiles for radii of clumps 1 and 3), halo modeled as Sérsic profile; magnification μ = 1.60 +0.01/-0.02

recipe.goal: Reduce JWST NIRSpec prism spectroscopy and extract emission line fluxes
recipe.method: Stage 1 JWST pipeline reduction followed by msaexp for wavelength calibration, background subtraction, Gaussian spatial profile extraction of 1D spectrum, spline continuum subtraction, and emission line fitting
key_parameters: R = 100 prism spectra, two three-shutter slits

recipe.goal: Image ALMA Band 7 and Band 8 continuum and measure Band 8 flux density and size
recipe.method: Image science archive calibrated visibilities in B7 (353 GHz) and B8 (465 GHz) using CASA tclean, and perform a 2D Gaussian fit on the B8 continuum image
key_parameters: natural weighting, 3σ cleaning threshold, multifrequency synthesis mode in all line-free channels

recipe.method: Evaluate magnification at target position using cluster-scale lens model constructed with Lenstool constrained by 303 multiple images with spectroscopic redshifts

recipe.goal: Fit cold dust SED to ALMA continuum detections and upper limits
recipe.method: Fit a Modified Blackbody (MBB) function plus nonthermal radio contribution to detections at 465 and 353 GHz and forced to reach the 3σ upper limit at 200 GHz, at fixed dust temperatures (T_dust = 60 K and 80 K)
key_parameters: T_dust fixed at 60 K and 80 K; MCMC with 20 chains, 2000 trials, burn-in phase of ~100
assumptions: k_0 = 0.45 cm^2 g^-1 at 250 GHz (Beelen et al. 2006), T_0 = 2.73 K for CMB heating/background, Chabrier (2003) IMF, continuum mean size from Tamura et al. (2023), nonthermal radio contribution following Algera et al. (2021)

recipe.goal: Perform optical-NIR SED and spectrophotometric fitting to infer stellar population properties and SFHs
recipe.method: Fit resolved and integrated photometry with DENSE BASIS (nonparametric SFH), and fit integrated NIRCam photometry + scaled NIRSpec spectrum with Bagpipes (double power-law and Iyer et al. 2019 nonparametric SFHs)
key_parameters: Fixed z = 8.31 in Bagpipes; parameter ranges and priors listed in Table A1
assumptions: Calzetti et al. (2000) dust attenuation curve, Chabrier (2003) IMF

recipe.goal: Derive ISM physical properties and AGN diagnostics from optical and FIR emission line ratios
recipe.method: Correct emission lines for dust using Hβ/Hδ and Calzetti law, deblend [O III]λ4363 from Hγ, compute T_e([O III]), ξ_ion, electron density (with PyNeb and ALMA [O III] 88 μm), oxygen abundance, ionization parameter, and compare line ratios on O32-R23, R2-R3, and [O III]λ4363 diagnostic diagrams
assumptions: Calzetti et al. (2000) extinction law, Case B recombination Hβ/Hδ = 3.78 for T_e = 1.6 x 10^4 K, T_e = 18000 ± 4000 K in PyNeb, solar oxygen abundance 12 + log(O/H) = 8.6

evidence.quote: We analyze the new continuum emission in B8 at 465 GHz, and by performing a 2D Gaussian fit, we derive a flux density of 254 ± 81 μJy and a peak flux of 199 ± 34 μJy (6σ detection).

evidence.quote: We analyze the new continuum emission in B8 at 465 GHz, and by performing a 2D Gaussian fit, we derive a flux density of 254 ± 81 μJy and a peak flux of 199 ± 34 μJy (6σ detection).
The source is barely resolved with a size of (0.52 ± 0.39) × (0.21 ± 0.31) arcsec 2 .
